Bacterial_Stalk_Rot.quote: The rind and the pith become soft, brown, and water-soaked.
The leaf tissue within the whorl and the growing point of the stem within the whorl are brown, wet, slimy.

Carbonum_Leaf_Spot.quote: Grayish tan lesions surrounded by a darker border first appear on lower leaf blades.
They may also occur on leaf sheaths and husks.

Common_Rust.quote: These pustules may appear on any above ground part of the plant, but are most abundant on the leaves.

Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma.quote: Corn stunt, as the name implies, results in stunted plants.
Younger leaves near the top of the plant are yellow.
The ears are small and do not fill properly leaving a large number of blank spaces on the ear.

Crazy_Top.quote: Crazy top-affected plants are distorted and/or stunted.
The leaves below the tassel may proliferate, resulting in a very bushy appearance of the top of the plant.

Diplodia_Stalk_Rot.quote: Plants affected by Diplodia stalk rot have shredded pith and die prematurely.
Numerous black dots, about the size of a pinhead or smaller, can be observed in the lower internodes.

Ear_Rots.quote: Dense white to gray mold that appears on and between the kernels at the base of the ear and progresses toward the tip.
Symptoms are a white to pink or salmon-colored, cottony mold that occurs on single or multiple kernels scattered or clustered on the ear.

Eyespot.quote: The spot is surrounded by a yellow 'halo' that can be seen clearly when the leaf is lighted from behind.
The first visible symptoms of eyespot are small, circular spots (1/16 inch to 1/8 inch diameter) that are water-soaked with yellow halos on leaves.

Fusarium_Disease.quote: Affected plants have shredded pith that may be a whitish-pink to salmon color.
Affected plants may be stunted, wilted, or have yellowed lower leaves.
brown to black discoloration of roots may be observed

General_And_Mixed_Stalk_Rots.quote: A healthy corn plant has white dense pith compared to a plant with stalk rot which has discolored and shredded pith.

When stalks are weakened by pathogens, the plant's ability to transport water and nutrients is reduced, which can reduce yield, and weakened stalks are also more susceptible to lodging before harvest.

Genetic_Flecking_Or_Striping.quote: Bright yellow to white interveinal striping running the length of leaves may be the result of 'genetic stripe'

Gray_Leaf_Spot.quote: The lesions (spots) caused by the fungal disease are first found on the lower leaves, but may spread to higher leaves as the disease progresses.

Head_Smut.quote: Forming on the tassels and ears, galls are at first covered with a thin layer of tissue that breaks open to expose the black spore masses.

Holcus_Spot.quote: Symptoms of holcus spot first appear as water-soaked, dark green lesions near the tips of lower leaves.

Leaf_Blight.quote: Early in the season, lower leaves usually show symptoms first. Later, symptoms can occasionally be found on upper leaves.

Leaf_Spot.quote: Symptoms first appear on lower leaves about two to three weeks before tasseling.

Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus.quote: leaf reddening or yellowing, leaf twisting and tearing, and chlorosis or clearing of the smallest visible leaf veins (vein banding)
plant stunting, shortening of upper internodes

Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus.quote: Infected plants have a stippled (small, discolored specks) mottle or mosaic of light and dark green that may develop into narrow streaks on the youngest leaves.
There may be a shortening of internodes causing a stunted, bunchy appearance of the plant.
may be barren or have small ears with kernel abortion.

Maize_Lethal_Necrosis.quote: Symptoms of the combination appear as a bright greenish-yellow leaf mottling that lasts until the end of the growing season.
Plants infected late in the season may exhibit poorly filled ears, have premature husk death, and lack leaf mosaic symptoms.

Maize_Streak_Virus.quote: the spots develop into narrow, white to yellow streaks that grow parallel to the leaf veins.

Northern_Leaf_Blight.quote: Symptoms usually appear first on the lower leaves.

Physoderma_Stalk_Rot.quote: These nodes are black and some pith rot may be present.

Smut.quote: Common smut galls can form on stalks, leaves, ears, and tassels; actively growing tissue is especially susceptible.

Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight.quote: Race T attacks leaves, husks, stalks, leaf sheaths, shanks, ears, and cobs.

Southern_Rust.quote: In severe cases, pustules may also develop on husks, leaf sheaths, and ear shanks.

Tar_Spot.quote: Tar spot appears as small, raised, black spots scattered across the upper and lower leaf surfaces.
When severe, stromata can even appear on husks and leaf sheaths.

Trichoderma_Ear_Rot.quote: It appears as dark green mold growing on or between kernels, often covering the entire ear.
